_doc: H4 raw-SQL audit ratchet — tenant-isolation epic file #12 (leak vector B7).
_why: Prisma $extends scoping does NOT touch $queryRaw*/$executeRaw*. Every raw-SQL site bypasses the tenant filter and must be manually reviewed for a businessId predicate. This file freezes the pre-existing sites (Phase-0 baseline). lint-raw-client.mjs (#11) fails the build if ANY file exceeds its sanctioned count or a new file introduces raw SQL — new raw SQL only lands by explicitly raising a row here (and being reviewed for tenant scoping). A count going DOWN is always allowed (ratchet).
_gate: This baseline gates Phase 2 (enforce): every site must be audited (reviewed for a WHERE business_id predicate) before SCOPED_PRISMA_ENFORCE=enforce ships. Until then a site is baseline-frozen but not yet certified tenant-safe.
_widened: 2026-07-21 (M-4a): the linter's walk root moved from server/src to the repo root, so scripts/, server/scripts/ and server/prisma/ are linted for the first time. server/scripts/backfill-money-paise.ts is the only file that surfaced. Its 8 sites are pre-existing and deliberately cross-tenant — it is a one-off rupees-to-paise migration that must rewrite every row in the table regardless of owner, so a business_id predicate would make it wrong, not safe. Frozen at its current count, NOT certified: the _gate above still applies before enforce ships.
_reviewed_2026_07_23: erasure.service.ts raised 4→6: the $executeRaw scrubs were already frozen; the new $queryRaw (SELECT DISTINCT businessId FROM ImportJob WHERE userId = $1) is scoped by the erased userId, NOT by business. This is a platform-wide DPDP erasure sweep that must span every business the user imported into — a business_id predicate would make it wrong, not safe (same rationale as backfill-money-paise). Raw SQL is deliberately chosen here so a future ImportJob scoped-models entry can never silently tenant-narrow the sweep and under-erase. Reviewed tenant-safe. (The +2 is 1 real query + 1 token from widening the TxLike Pick to include '$queryRaw'.)
_reviewed_2026_07_26: dashboard/trend.ts added with 2 sites: daily sales (Document) and daily payments (Payment) bucketed by date_trunc('day'), which Prisma groupBy cannot express. Both carry an explicit "businessId" = $1 predicate as their first WHERE term and select only aggregate sums for that business. Reviewed tenant-safe. They replace hardcoded mock numbers that were being shown to real users as their own sales.
_ratchet_lowered: 2026-07-21: the B7 counter now skips comment lines. The 2026-07-19 baseline was seeded by a whole-file grep, so it counted the token inside prose and over-stated 7 files by 9 sites — campaign-segment.service.ts scored 3 while containing no raw SQL at all, its entire count coming from a header that says the unsafe variants are banned. Every over-stated site was live headroom: real raw SQL could have landed in those files without tripping the ratchet. Counts re-derived from non-comment lines.
_reviewed_2026_07_26: server/prisma/e2e-reset.ts added at 2 sites (SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables; TRUNCATE ... CASCADE). Deliberately and necessarily cross-tenant: it wipes an entire throwaway E2E database, so a business_id predicate would make it wrong, not safe (same rationale as backfill-money-paise). Raw SQL is also the only way to derive the table list from the catalogue rather than hardcoding it — the integration suite lists 27 of 150 tables by hand, which leaves ~120 dirty between runs. Cannot touch real data: refuses unless the DB name ends _test/_e2e AND NODE_ENV!==production. Reviewed tenant-safe.
